title: unified-rollouts: enhanced safety guards and observability for shadow-canary autorollback
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Adds conservative safety guards and expanded observability for the unified rollouts shadow+canary autorollback flow. Motivation: we observed two incidents where a transient metric spike in shadow traffic caused premature autorollbacks during multi-stage canary rollouts. This PR hardens the decision surface to reduce false positives while preserving automated rollback for real regressions.

What it does (high level):
- Adds minimum sample-size gating and transient smoothing window for shadow metrics used by autorollback (latency, error-rate, hallucination-score).
- Implements multi-metric voting (majority of three metrics) with configurable weights and per-metric threshold buckets.
- Introduces a staging-window delay before an autorollback action is taken (configurable, defaults to 3 minutes).
- Adds cooldown and backoff for repeated rollbacks to avoid oscillation.
- Exposes new observability signals: rollout:autorollback_decision, rollout:metric_windows, rollout:sample_counts, rollout:rollback_cooldown_active.
- Adds dashboard tiles and alert rules (SLO-aligned) and tracing tags to link rollback decisions to request traces and model hash.
- Minor API addition to rollout spec: safetyGuards block (backward compatible, defaulted).

Design notes:
- We keep the runtime decision path cheap: gating calculations are vectorized and cached per-rollout-window. New computations use existing metrics ingestion stream (no extra pull).
- Default behavior is opt-in via server default; existing rollout specs without safetyGuards still get reasonable defaults to avoid breaking existing flows.
- Config knobs are exposed in the Console for Dedicated/Private customers behind a feature flag.

Tests and validation:
- Unit tests for gating logic and voting combinator (coverage added).
- Integration tests simulate shadow + canary traffic with injected metric spikes to verify no false autorollbacks under transient noise and correct rollback on persistent regressions.
- E2E in perf-canary with a staged rollout (staging -> 10% -> 50%) ran with chaos injected; metrics and dashboards validated.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add safety guard implementation in controller
- [x] Add metrics and tracing tags
- [x] Add integration+unit tests
- [x] Add Console knobs and defaulting logic
- [x] Update rollout schema and validation
- [x] Run perf-canary and e2e stability tests
- [x] Docs + release notes

Backward compatibility and rollout:
- New rollout spec field is optional. Platform defaults protect existing customers. We will ship behind a gradual feature flag and enable platform-wide after 2 weeks of canary monitoring. Rollback action remains the same API; only the decision calculus changes.

Related: ENG-3412 (reduce false-positives for autorollback), ENG-3478 (observability for rollouts), previous PRs pr-131204 and pr-150321 for baseline autorollback behavior.

Notes for reviewers: pay special attention to the gating thresholds in controllers/rollout/safety_guards.go and to the integration test harness where we simulate noisy telemetry. The metrics names are intentionally short to keep storage overhead low (see metrics/rollout_metrics.go).
